structural_facts.gtin_single_owner: idx_product_identifiers_canonical_gtin14_owner is a UNIQUE index on canonical_gtin14: one valid GTIN can belong to exactly one product row in the whole catalogue. A KEEP-BOTH pair can therefore carry the barcode on only one entry.
structural_facts.scan_lookup: src/lib/scan/identifier-lookup.ts resolves a barcode to the owning product and filters out inactive/discontinued products, so a GTIN left on a retired entry would break scanning.

steps_per_retired_row: products: is_chaarlie_recommended=false, lifecycle_status='discontinued' (and is_active=false as in the 8 existing tombstones)
move user_products.catalog_product_id to the keeper where owners exist (Pantene f8f3b51d has 1)
move product_identifiers rows (GTIN) from retired to keeper where the retired row owns them (Midnight oil -> leave_in)
keep spec/protocol/evidence rows in place: the audit treats a retired + superseded row as a tombstone and skips completeness checks (isRetiredSuperseded in src/lib/catalog-authority/audit.ts)
retirement_mechanism.do_not: Do not delete rows; do not use personal_plan_product_search_dispositions (that is for search-gap products, not duplicates).
caveats: All 8 existing replaced_by edges are same-category; the three KEEP-ONE pairs here are cross-category (shampoo->deep_cleansing, oil->leave_in, leave_in->oil). Schema (CHECK source<>target only) and audit allow it, but src/lib/catalog-authority/repair.ts slices are category-bounded and the 2026-08-15 preflight demanded same category; Balea shampoo->deep_cleansing spans two slices.
selection.ts already excludes any product with an outgoing replaced_by edge from recommendation.
